**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, RENEWAL).**

What I found:

- **Term/renewal mechanics (compliant, better than preferred):** § 2 (p0011) is an evergreen term running "until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6," and § 6(a) allows either party to terminate for convenience on 15 days' notice when no SOW is outstanding. There is no auto-renewal, no renewal term length and no non-renewal notice window anywhere in the document (no hits for "renew"/"successive"). Exit is easier than our preferred position, so I did **not** add renewal mechanics.
- **Renewal/roll-over pricing (fails fallback):** § 3(b) gives Contractor an uncapped unilateral right to "change rates with 30 days notice," with no annual frequency limit and no protection for in-flight Statements of Work — exactly the period when Company cannot use the § 6(a) convenience exit. That defeats the rule's price-predictability limb (preferred: lesser of CPI and 3%; fallback: ≤ 5%).

Redline (validated ok:true, modelled on `seed-renewal`): rate changes limited to once per twelve months, capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%, and not applicable to any outstanding Statement of Work without our consent — with 5% flagged in the comment as an acceptable fallback.
